question: Is there flooding near 80 Pioneer Street, Brooklyn right now?

plan.rationale: The query asks about current flooding conditions at a specific street address.

claims.text: This address is mapped within FEMA flood zone AE, a Special Flood Hazard Area, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970192F, effective 2007.
Six FloodNet community sensors within 600 meters have logged nine above-curb flood events in the last three years, with a peak depth recorded of 89 mm.

Sixty NYC 311 flood-related complaints have been filed within 200 meters of this location in the last five years, with the most common descriptor being Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC).
The latest tide reading at The Battery, NY was 4.23 ft above mean lower low water (MLLW), observed on 2026-09-26 at 17:18, which is 2.36 ft higher than the predicted tide.
There are three active NWS alerts at this point: Coastal Flood Warning (Severe), High Surf Advisory (Minor), and Rip Current Statement (Moderate).

Flood Resilience at NYCHA, as detailed on page 74 of the document, includes lessons learned from the Hurricane Sandy Disaster Recovery Program, specifically addressing sites like ASTORIA, BARUCH, BEACH 41ST STREET, CAMPOS PLAZA II, CAREY GARDENS, CARLTON MANOR, CONEY ISLAND (SITE 8), CONEY ISLAND HOUSES, CONEY ISLAND IB, EAST RIVER, GOWANUS, GRAVESEND, HABER, HAMMEL, ISAACS, LA GUARDIA, LAVANBURG HOMES, and LINCOLN HO.

The MTA Climate Resilience Roadmap (October 2025 update) on page 11 notes that the stretch of 4 Avenue Brooklyn between Union St and 36 St in the Gowanus neighborhood is served by five stations impacted by heavy rainfall, highlighting the need for city action due to chronic flooding in the area.

The NYC Comptroller’s report ‘Is NYC Ready for Rain?’ (2024) on page 38 references the Ophelia After-Action Report from the MTA (October 2023) concerning service response and resilience planning for flash flood events.
